lines.text: Lesson nineteen, and the start of Phase 5: scalping and risk management.
lines.say: Lesson nineteen, and the start of Phase five: scalping and risk management.

lines.text: First question: what is scalping?
lines.say: First question: what is scalping?

lines.text: So far you've learned to read candles, timeframes, trends, zones and volume.
lines.say: So far you've learned to read candles, timeframes, trends, zones and volume.

lines.text: Now: how do short-term traders use them? And what does it really cost?
lines.say: Now: how do short-term traders use them? And what does it really cost?

lines.text: Let's look honestly, costs and all.
lines.say: Let's look honestly, costs and all.

lines.text: Scalping means trying to profit from small price moves, in trades that last minutes.
lines.say: Scalping means trying to profit from small price moves, in trades that last minutes.

lines.text: Sometimes only seconds. Then the trader exits and waits for the next one.
lines.say: Sometimes only seconds. Then the trader exits and waits for the next one.

lines.text: Think of a stall that makes many small sales, each with a thin margin.
lines.say: Think of a stall that makes many small sales, each with a thin margin.

lines.text: Thin margins mean costs matter a lot.
lines.say: Thin margins mean costs matter a lot.

lines.text: Here's a fictional 15-minute chart of 1-minute candles.
lines.say: Here's a fictional fifteen-minute chart of one-minute candles.

lines.text: A scalper might notice two things. These are observations, not signals.
lines.say: A scalper might notice two things. These are observations, not signals.

lines.text: One: price dips to a support zone and holds. Two: a sudden spike on thin volume.
lines.say: One: price dips to a support zone and holds. Two: a sudden spike on thin volume.

lines.text: Say a demo long opens at 60,000 and closes 4 minutes later at 60,120.
lines.say: Say a demo long opens at sixty thousand and closes four minutes later at sixty thousand one hundred twenty.

lines.text: Held for 4 minutes. Price move: +120 USDT. It could have failed.
lines.say: Held for four minutes. Price move: plus one hundred twenty U-S-D-T. It could have failed.

lines.text: Now the costs. The position is 0.1 BTC: 6,000 USDT at 60,000.
lines.say: Now the costs. The position is zero point one B-T-C: six thousand U-S-D-T at sixty thousand.

lines.text: Gross profit: 0.1 × 120 = 12.00 USDT.
lines.say: Gross profit: zero point one times one hundred twenty equals twelve U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Fees at an example 0.05% each side: 3.00 to enter, 3.01 to exit.
lines.say: Fees at an example zero point zero five percent each side: three to enter, three point zero one to exit.

lines.text: Net: 12.00 − 3.00 − 3.01 = 5.99 USDT. Half the move went to fees.
lines.say: Net: twelve minus three minus three point zero one equals five point nine nine U-S-D-T. Half the move went to fees.

lines.text: A losing scalp pays fees too, so the loss gets bigger.
lines.say: A losing scalp pays fees too, so the loss gets bigger.

lines.text: Trade frequency is how many trades you make in a period.
lines.say: Trade frequency is how many trades you make in a period.

lines.text: Each round trip here costs about 6 USDT in fees.
lines.say: Each round trip here costs about six U-S-D-T in fees.

lines.text: Twenty trades in a day: about 120 USDT in fees, win or lose.
lines.say: Twenty trades in a day: about one hundred twenty U-S-D-T in fees, win or lose.

lines.text: And every trade is one more chance to be wrong.
lines.say: And every trade is one more chance to be wrong.

lines.text: More trades is not more profit.
lines.say: More trades is not more profit.

lines.text: Execution quality is how close your fill is to the price you expected.
lines.say: Execution quality is how close your fill is to the price you expected.

lines.text: Say you slip 10 USDT getting in and 10 getting out.
lines.say: Say you slip ten U-S-D-T getting in and ten getting out.

lines.text: Our 120 move shrinks to 100, before fees.
lines.say: Our one hundred twenty move shrinks to one hundred, before fees.

lines.text: When moves are small, spread and slippage take a big share.
lines.say: When moves are small, spread and slippage take a big share.

lines.text: How does scalping compare with holding for days or weeks?
lines.say: How does scalping compare with holding for days or weeks?

lines.text: Scalping: minutes, many trades, costs are a big share of each small move.
lines.say: Scalping: minutes, many trades, costs are a big share of each small move.

lines.text: Longer holding: fewer trades, bigger moves, but more time exposed to news.
lines.say: Longer holding: fewer trades, bigger moves, but more time exposed to news.

lines.text: Neither is safe. Both can lose money.
lines.say: Neither is safe. Both can lose money.

lines.text: A note on XORA. It looks at about 10 to 15 minutes of recent price for context.
lines.say: A note on Zora. It looks at about ten to fifteen minutes of recent price for context.

lines.text: That is an analysis horizon. It is not a time you must hold a trade.
lines.say: That is an analysis horizon. It is not a time you must hold a trade.

lines.text: And it is not a promise of where price will be in 15 minutes.
lines.say: And it is not a promise of where price will be in fifteen minutes.

lines.text: Some moments are simply not good for trading.
lines.say: Some moments are simply not good for trading.

lines.text: Very thin markets. Wild news spikes. Fees bigger than the expected move.
lines.say: Very thin markets. Wild news spikes. Fees bigger than the expected move.

lines.text: No clear reason, no stop, or you're tired, upset or chasing a loss.
lines.say: No clear reason, no stop, or you're tired, upset or chasing a loss.

lines.text: In all of these, NO_TRADE is the right call. Waiting is a skill.
lines.say: In all of these, no trade is the right call. Waiting is a skill.

lines.text: Your turn. A scalp's expected move is 60 USDT per BTC, at a price of 60,000.
lines.say: Your turn. A scalp's expected move is sixty U-S-D-T per B-T-C, at a price of sixty thousand.

lines.text: Round-trip fees are 0.10%. Is it worth taking? Pause and think.
lines.say: Round-trip fees are zero point one percent. Is it worth taking? Pause and think.

lines.text: Fees: 60,000 × 0.10% = 60 USDT per BTC. The move only covers the fees.
lines.say: Fees: sixty thousand times zero point one percent equals sixty U-S-D-T per B-T-C. The move only covers the fees.

lines.text: Even before slippage, it's zero. NO_TRADE makes sense.
lines.say: Even before slippage, it's zero. No trade makes sense.

lines.text: Before you try scalping, even in demo, know the limits.
lines.say: Before you try scalping, even in demo, know the limits.

lines.text: It is not easy money. Many small losses and fees add up fast.
lines.say: It is not easy money. Many small losses and fees add up fast.

lines.text: Fast decisions bring mistakes, and leverage makes every loss bigger.
lines.say: Fast decisions bring mistakes, and leverage makes every loss bigger.

lines.text: Practise in demo first. NO_TRADE is always allowed.
lines.say: Practise in demo first. No trade is always allowed.

lines.text: Let's recap.
lines.say: Let's recap.

lines.text: Scalping aims for small moves in short trades: seconds to minutes.
lines.say: Scalping aims for small moves in short trades: seconds to minutes.

lines.text: Fees, spread and slippage take a big share of small moves.
lines.say: Fees, spread and slippage take a big share of small moves.

lines.text: XORA's 10 to 15 minutes is context, not a holding rule. NO_TRADE is allowed.
lines.say: Zora's ten to fifteen minutes is context, not a holding rule. No trade is allowed.

lines.text: Check yourself: a move of 60 USDT per BTC, fees of 60. Worth it?
lines.say: Check yourself: a move of sixty U-S-D-T per B-T-C, fees of sixty. Worth it?

lines.text: No. It only covers fees, before slippage. Waiting is the better call.
lines.say: No. It only covers fees, before slippage. Waiting is the better call.

lines.text: Well done! Next up: evaluating an entry opportunity. See you in lesson twenty.
lines.say: Well done! Next up: evaluating an entry opportunity. See you in lesson twenty.
